samples.summary: gate 1's "newest CI run wins" rule (now pinned by the new test) can fail open when a SHA has more than one CI run
samples.evidence: `ciPassed` (mark-ready.mjs:133-137) filters to runs named "CI", sorts by `created_at` descending and returns `runs[0].conclusion === "success"`, ignoring every other CI run for the SHA. The new test (mark-ready.test.mjs:211-247) enshrines this as the intended semantics via fabricated fixtures where a re-run has a later `created_at`. In the real Actions API a re-run does NOT create a new workflow run — it adds a `run_attempt` to the existing run, keeping `created_at` — so the only way a single SHA has two CI runs is when CI is triggered twice for it (e.g. push + pull_request, or a workflow_dispatch alongside), and in that case a RED CI run for the head SHA is silently ignored whenever a differently-triggered CI run created later is green. Gate 1 is the "the tests passed" gate, so this promotes a PR whose CI is not entirely green. Reading the newest run is also nondeterministic if `created_at` is absent/invalid on any run (`new Date(undefined)` → NaN comparator → unspecified sort order), and there is no `status === "completed"` check, so an in-flight later attempt is judged on a stale conclusion field.

verdict.reason: The sort/runs[0] code is present as described (scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:125-138), but the failure mechanism the finding relies on is not reachable in this repo, and its auxiliary claims are already guarded. (a) The finding's own premise is that the only way one SHA gets two CI runs is a double trigger (push + pull_request, or a workflow_dispatch alongside). .github/workflows/ci.yml:4-28 is the only workflow named "CI" (grep of ^name: across .github/workflows) and has NO workflow_dispatch; push is restricted to branches:["main"], and a merge_group run's head_sha is the throwaway gh-readonly-queue merge commit, not the PR head (ci.yml:11-23). So no differently-triggered competing CI run can exist for a PR head SHA. (b) The multi-run cases that can occur (pull_request default type "reopened", or a force-push back to a prior SHA) are re-evaluations of the same SHA - exactly what newest-wins exists for (mark-ready.mjs:135 comment; test.mjs:236-246 pins the converse) and what GitHub itself does for required contexts (latest result per context wins). (c) "No status === completed check, so an in-flight run is judged on a stale conclusion": an in-flight run reports conclusion null, which fails === "success" and therefore fails CLOSED - asserted by the pre-existing test at mark-ready.test.mjs:174-181. (d) "new Date(undefined) -> NaN comparator": line 136 is new Date(b.created_at ?? 0) - new Date(a.created_at ?? 0), so absent/null yields new Date(0), deterministic. (e) Impact is further bounded: this script never merges - it only flips draft to ready, relabels, and comments (mark-ready.mjs:22-25, 205, 232-234, 261); merge authority is branch protection's required contexts (ci.yml:15-17). What remains is a policy preference (all runs green vs latest run green), not a reachable correctness fail-open.
